record.paper_title: Semantic Subtyping: Challenges, Perspectives, and Open Problems
record.original_question: Can the semantic-subtyping methodology be extended fruitfully to dependent type systems, such as π-calculus systems with channel-dependent types or the first-order dependent type theory λΠ, in a way that yields a genuinely semantic characterization of subtyping rather than one tied primarily to syntactic normalization rules?

evidence.quote: As a final research direction for the semantic subtyping we want to hint at the research on dependent types.
It would then be interesting to check whether the semantic subtyping approach yields a more semantic characterisation of the subtyping relation for dependent types.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. The semantic subtyping methodology defines the subtype relation between types by first interpreting types as subsets of a suitable set-theoretic model and then declaring T ≤ S to hold whenever the interpretation of T is contained in the interpretation of S. This approach allows boolean combinators (union, intersection, negation) to be given their natural set-theoretic meaning, and has been worked out for various typed calculi including λ-calculi with arrow, product and boolean type connectives, and the π-calculus with channel types.

Two target settings.
(1) A π-calculus with channel-dependent types: a typed asynchronous (or synchronous) π-calculus in which the type of values that may be communicated along a channel can depend on previously transmitted values, so that channel types take the form Π(x:T)·U(x) and similarly for received values.
(2) The first-order dependent type theory λΠ (the LF-style pure type system with kinds of the form Π(x:A)·K), in which type families may be indexed by terms.

In both settings, the conventional subtyping relation is typically defined inductively by syntactic rules whose key clauses rely on β- (and possibly η-) normalization of dependent type expressions.

Problem. Construct, for at least one of the two settings above:
(a) a set-theoretic (or otherwise model-theoretic) interpretation [[·]] of dependent types as subsets of some structured domain, taking proper account of the dependency on terms;
(b) a subtyping relation defined semantically by [[T]] ⊆ [[S]] (uniformly in the dependent parameters);
(c) a sound and complete syntactic characterization of this semantic relation, together with a decision procedure when types are restricted to a decidable fragment;
such that the resulting subtyping relation is a genuinely semantic notion — not merely a reformulation of the syntactic rules based on normalization — and such that it conservatively extends the standard semantic subtyping for the non-dependent fragment while remaining adequate for typing the corresponding calculus.

Equivalently, decide whether the semantic subtyping methodology can be extended fruitfully to dependent type systems of the above kind so as to yield a characterization of subtyping that is intrinsically semantic rather than tied primarily to syntactic normalization.
artifact.status_search_result: Search reveals related but distinct work: semantic subtyping for the π-calculus with channel types (Castagna, De Nicola, Varacca) and various studies of subtyping for dependent types (Aspinall; subtyping in λΠ-modulo). However, no source clearly establishes a fully developed semantic-subtyping framework for π-calculus with channel-dependent types or for first-order dependent λΠ that yields a genuinely semantic (rather than normalization-based) characterization. The status of the question therefore appears unresolved based on available sources.

status_evidence.title: Semantic subtyping for the pi-calculus
status_evidence.snippet: A semantic characterisation of channel types has been proposed and used to derive a subtyping relation for the pi-calculus.
status_evidence.claim: Semantic subtyping has been developed for the (non-dependent) π-calculus with channel types, but the cited work does not address channel-dependent types.

status_evidence.title: Subtyping Dependent Types (Aspinall)
status_evidence.snippet: Research has been conducted on combining subtyping with dependent types. The system λP (λΠ) underlies LF.
status_evidence.claim: Subtyping for dependent type systems including λΠ has been studied syntactically, without providing a set-theoretic semantic-subtyping interpretation.

status_evidence.title: Objects and Subtyping in the Lambda-Pi-Calculus Modulo
status_evidence.snippet: The lambda-Pi-calculus modulo, an extension with rewriting, has been used to embed Object Calculus and translation of subtyping.
status_evidence.claim: Existing subtyping treatments for λΠ-modulo are based on rewriting/normalization rather than a semantic set-theoretic interpretation.
